doc.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019

title: Becoming Bobby Short's musical director
summary: Schoenberg lists his teaching and radio jobs, then in 1997 becomes Bobby Short's musical director after a joke about a big band.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So to put it all together, so I was teaching at Manhattan, doing the Sirius Satellite Radio show, Juilliard was just about to start a jazz program, and I was going to teach there. And in 1997 I became Bobby Short’s musical director. So Bobby had had a trio for many, many years, famously, at the Café Carlyle. And we were in the wings once at Jazz at Lincoln Center on the benefit concert, we were both appearing. And I jokingly said, because I knew him through a woman named Jean Bach, and they were very good friends, and so I got to see that world, which is another world. And I said to Bobby © Fillius Jazz Archive -27-
